text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thousands of fans of dead Afrobeat musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti braved hot sun for a glimpse of their hero's embalmed body.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani said all distressed banks in the country would have been liquidated by now were it not for the fact that they owe the central bank about 13 billion naira.
- Investments worth over three billion naira are at risk since the government changed the rules for operators of Very Small Aperture Terminal (V-SAT) communications.
- Guinea will supply a substantial proportion of bauxite destined for Nigeria's ALSCON aluminium smelter, which is expected to open near the end of this year.
- Over $120 million has been spent by the National Maritime Agency over the past 10 years to help Nigerian shipping companies acquire vessels.

- The government has approved 19 banks to handle the accounts of state-run bodies, whenever the central bank gives up the job. The names of the banks, who will handle accounts estimated to be worth 44 billion naira, are not yet known.
- Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company has intensified efforts to find oil in northern Bauchi state.
